description: Active subdomain-takeover VERIFICATION PASS that turns the heuristic VERIFY tier into a concrete verdict (VULNERABLE / NOT_VULNERABLE / INCONCLUSIVE) with human-readable evidence, plus the full backend wiring, CSV columns (positions 13-14), and frontend verdict badge/filter/count/evidence. Independent of FEAT-002 at the logic level; both touch SubdomainResult, analyze_subdomain, download_csv, and static/index.html, so FEAT-002 is sequenced after this to avoid merge churn in the shared files.
steps: In main.py near CLOUD_RESOURCE_PATTERNS (~line 377) add verdict constants: VERDICT_VULNERABLE='VULNERABLE', VERDICT_NOT_VULNERABLE='NOT_VULNERABLE', VERDICT_INCONCLUSIVE='INCONCLUSIVE', VERIFY_HTTP_TIMEOUT=5.0.

Add `async def verify_takeover(result, probe_client, sem) -> dict` AFTER check_takeover (ends ~line 1162) and BEFORE analyze_subdomain (~line 1164). Return {'verdict': <str>, 'evidence': <str>}. Only act when result['takeover_risk'] in {'VERIFY','HIGH'}; otherwise return {'verdict':'','evidence':''}. Compute final_target = (cname_chain[-1] if cname_chain else cname); provider = _match_cloud_resource(final_target). Resolve the TARGET's own DNS via resolve_dns_detailed(final_target) to get target IPs + target dns_status (NXDOMAIN-of-target signal).

SSRF guard inside verify_takeover: if the target resolved to IP(s) and none satisfy _is_safe_public_ip, DO NOT probe; return INCONCLUSIVE with evidence noting the probe was skipped by the SSRF guard. Bound every probe with `async with sem` and pass VERIFY_HTTP_TIMEOUT; probe the target endpoint via check_http(probe_client, final_target) (reuse already-fetched body where equivalent). Wrap the whole body in try/except that returns INCONCLUSIVE with the error noted — never raise, never crash the job.

Per-provider decision inside verify_takeover (provider names from CLOUD_RESOURCE_PATTERNS): AWS S3 -> body 'NoSuchBucket' => VULNERABLE, 200 listing or 'AccessDenied' => NOT_VULNERABLE; AWS ELB -> target dns_status RESOLVED => NOT_VULNERABLE with evidence that an ELB name is NOT attacker-choosable (unlike S3/GitHub), likely internal/down (503=no healthy targets), confirm ownership in AWS, and target NXDOMAIN => INCONCLUSIVE with evidence 'ELB target no longer resolves; cannot be re-registered by an attacker via a chosen name, but confirm in AWS'; AWS CloudFront -> 'Bad request'/'ERROR: The request could not be satisfied' => INCONCLUSIVE only (never claim VULNERABLE); GitHub Pages -> "There isn't a GitHub Pages site here" => VULNERABLE else NOT_VULNERABLE; Heroku -> 'No such app' => VULNERABLE else NOT_VULNERABLE; Azure (web apps/cloud app/traffic manager/blob) -> VULNERABLE only when target name itself NXDOMAIN + known 404 signature else NOT_VULNERABLE/INCONCLUSIVE; GCP (storage.googleapis.com/appspot.com) -> not-found signature => VULNERABLE else NOT_VULNERABLE; Fastly -> 'Fastly error: unknown domain' => VULNERABLE else NOT_VULNERABLE; default/unknown => INCONCLUSIVE listing observations. GENERAL RULE: VULNERABLE requires (a) a provider resource-does-not-exist/claimable body/status signature, or (b) target hostname NXDOMAIN for a user-chosen-name provider (S3, GitHub, Heroku, Azure sites, GCP, Fastly). For ELB/CloudFront prefer NOT_VULNERABLE/INCONCLUSIVE and say why in evidence. evidence must cite the exact observation (status, matched signature, NXDOMAIN-of-target).
Add `takeover_verdict: str` and `takeover_evidence: str` to the SubdomainResult TypedDict (~line 441).

Wire into analyze_subdomain (~line 1164): after check_takeover returns, call verify_takeover ONLY when risk in {'VERIFY','HIGH'}, passing result data + probe_client + the SAME sem already in scope (no new semaphore, no unbounded fan-out). Set takeover_verdict/takeover_evidence on BOTH the invalid-hostname early-return (set to '') and the main return. If verdict == VULNERABLE you MAY promote takeover_risk to 'HIGH' (do so and note it in evidence); otherwise keep takeover_risk (VERIFY stays VERIFY with a 'checked: not vulnerable (ELB name not claimable)'-style evidence). Non-flagged rows get verdict='' and evidence=''.

In _summarize (~line 1609) add vulnerable = sum(1 for r in results if r.get('takeover_verdict') == 'VULNERABLE') and include 'vulnerable': vulnerable in the returned dict (keep existing keys incl. verify).

Append CSV columns in CSV_COLUMNS (~line 1636): add 'takeover_verdict' then 'takeover_evidence' at positions 13 and 14 (first 12 unchanged). In the download_csv writer loop append _csv_safe(r.get('takeover_verdict','')) and _csv_safe(r.get('takeover_evidence','')).

Update tests/test_api.py SubdomainResult(...) fixture to include takeover_verdict and takeover_evidence; extend test_download_csv_header to expect takeover_verdict at index 12 and takeover_evidence at index 13 (header length grows — coordinate the exact length with FEAT-002 which adds dns_records at index 14; if FEAT-002 is not yet merged, assert len==14 here and FEAT-002 bumps it to 15).

Frontend static/index.html: add verdictBadge(v) next to riskBadge (~line 493) whitelisting VULNERABLE(red)/NOT_VULNERABLE(green 'Not vulnerable')/INCONCLUSIVE(grey 'Inconclusive'); any other value => '' (blank). Add a 'Verdict' <th> after the Risk header (~line 222) and a matching <td> in renderTable rendering verdictBadge(r.takeover_verdict) with r.takeover_evidence on a title= attribute via escapeHtml. Add a data-filter='vulnerable' button in #filterBtns (~line 196) and `case 'vulnerable': return r.takeover_verdict === 'VULNERABLE';` in applyFilters (~line 454). Add a red 'Vulnerable (confirmed)' summary card with id cardVulnerable near cardVerify (~line 164), set from data.vulnerable || 0 in the summary render (~line 414). Never innerHTML raw server data; use escapeHtml + the fixed whitelist exactly like riskBadge.

Add tests/test_verify_active.py (respx + monkeypatch, offline, following tests/test_active.py patterns): (a) ELB target that still RESOLVES -> NOT_VULNERABLE, evidence mentions ELB/not-claimable (gitlab/openproject case) — monkeypatch resolve_dns_detailed on the ELB target to RESOLVED; (b) GitHub Pages body "There isn't a GitHub Pages site here" -> VULNERABLE (respx-mock the probe); (c) S3 'NoSuchBucket' -> VULNERABLE and S3 200 listing -> NOT_VULNERABLE; (d) SSRF regression: monkeypatch target resolution to a private IP, assert no probe issued and verdict INCONCLUSIVE/skipped; (e) via analyze_subdomain, a non-flagged subdomain gets empty verdict/evidence.
acceptance_criteria: verify_takeover exists, is bounded by the passed Semaphore, routes all fetches through probe_client behind _is_safe_public_ip, and never raises (errors -> INCONCLUSIVE).
An ELB target that still resolves yields NOT_VULNERABLE with evidence explaining ELB names are not attacker-claimable (the gitlab/openproject result).
A GitHub Pages 'There isn't a GitHub Pages site here' body yields VULNERABLE; an S3 NoSuchBucket yields VULNERABLE; an S3 200 listing yields NOT_VULNERABLE.
A target resolving to a private/metadata IP is never probed and yields INCONCLUSIVE (SSRF regression holds).
Non-flagged subdomains carry takeover_verdict='' and takeover_evidence=''.
_summarize returns a 'vulnerable' count; results JSON exposes it.
CSV header contains takeover_verdict and takeover_evidence appended after dns_status; first 12 columns unchanged in order; both new cells pass through _csv_safe.
Frontend shows a Verdict badge (whitelisted 3 strings, blank otherwise), evidence on hover, a Vulnerable filter button, and a Vulnerable count card — all XSS-safe.
All 130 baseline tests still pass and the new verify tests pass.
findings: FEAT-001 complete. CSV header is now 14 columns in this exact order: [subdomain(0), ip_addresses(1), cname(2), http_status(3), https_status(4), sources(5), resolved(6), alive(7), takeover_risk(8), takeover_service(9), takeover_detail(10), dns_status(11), takeover_verdict(12), takeover_evidence(13)]. The first 12 (indices 0-11) are the fixed backward-compatible contract and MUST NOT be reordered. FEAT-002 should APPEND 'dns_records' at index 14 (do NOT insert before index 14) and bump CSV length assertions from 14 to 15 in tests/test_api.py (test_download_csv_header) and tests/test_security.py (test_csv_download_neutralizes_injection). New SubdomainResult TypedDict fields added by FEAT-001: 'takeover_verdict' (str: 'VULNERABLE'|'NOT_VULNERABLE'|'INCONCLUSIVE'|'' ) and 'takeover_evidence' (str) — both placed AFTER takeover_detail and BEFORE 'resolved' in the TypedDict and must be set on every SubdomainResult(...) call (both analyze_subdomain returns set them; non-flagged rows get ''). FEAT-002 should add 'dns_records' AFTER takeover_evidence in the TypedDict to keep ordering coherent. New backend symbols: VERDICT_VULNERABLE/VERDICT_NOT_VULNERABLE/VERDICT_INCONCLUSIVE constants, VERIFY_HTTP_TIMEOUT=5.0, and `async def verify_takeover(result, probe_client, sem) -> dict` (sits between check_takeover and analyze_subdomain). _summarize now also returns 'vulnerable' (count of takeover_verdict=='VULNERABLE'); job_results JSON exposes it. Frontend static/index.html additions: verdictBadge(v) (whitelist VULNERABLE/NOT_VULNERABLE/INCONCLUSIVE, blank otherwise) next to riskBadge; a 'Verdict' <th> inserted AFTER the Risk header and a matching <td> (verdictBadge + escapeHtml'd evidence title) AFTER the Risk cell and BEFORE the Live cell in renderTable; data-filter='vulnerable' button; 'vulnerable' case in applyFilters; cardVulnerable summary card set from data.vulnerable||0. If FEAT-002 adds a column/cell to the results table, insert it relative to these (e.g. a DNS-records cell can go after the CNAME cell). New test file tests/test_verify_active.py (10 tests). Full suite now 140 passed.
